correctness.rationale: In a complete multipartite graph, a nonempty set dominates exactly when it meets at least two parts or equals one whole part; for size at least two it is connected exactly when it meets at least two parts. Given connected dominating \(D\) of size \(s\), if the complement has fewer than \(s\) vertices it cannot contain an equal-size rival; if it meets two parts and has at least \(s\) vertices it contains a dominating \(s\)-subset; if it lies in one part, an equal-size dominating subset exists exactly when the complement is that whole part of size \(s\). The minimization cases then follow. The inspected verifier exhausts all multipartite profiles through order ten and every subset, matching both criterion and formula.
